title: One Word on a Robot: What Really Drives a Scientist
title_zh: 一台机器人身上的一个词：真正驱动科学家的是什么
intro_zh: 本文约549词，CET-4难度。文章以火星车“好奇号”的命名为例，说明科学家的好奇心更多是有耐心的观察、对意外现象的追问和对自身偏见的警惕，并配有彭齐亚斯与威尔逊、凯库勒、居里夫人等真实事例。正文含6个四级核心词（好奇心、观察、耐心、意外的、证据、怀疑）。

paragraphs.en: In 2009, a twelve-year-old girl named Clara Ma won a national essay contest with a few short paragraphs. Her prize was unusual: she got to name a robot. The machine was a car-sized laboratory that would soon travel to Mars and never come back. Clara chose one word — curiosity. Her reason was simple. Science, she wrote, is not about knowing everything. It is about wanting to know more.
paragraphs.zh: 2009年，一个名叫克拉拉·马的十二岁女孩凭一篇短短的文章赢得了全国作文比赛。她的奖品很特别：她可以给一台机器人命名。那台机器是一座汽车大小的实验室，很快将飞往火星，并且一去不回。克拉拉选了一个词——好奇。她的理由很简单：科学不是无所不知，而是想知道得更多。

paragraphs.en: That word describes a real working habit rather than a personality type. When we picture a scientist, we imagine a white coat, a microscope and a sudden shout of discovery. In fact, most of the job looks dull. It is observing the same detail again, cleaning instruments, and recording numbers that nobody will read for years. Curiosity in daily life is mostly patience with small things.
paragraphs.zh: 这个词描述的是一种真实的工作习惯，而不是一种性格类型。我们想象中的科学家，是白大褂、显微镜，还有突然的一声“发现了”。事实上，这份工作的大部分内容看起来很枯燥：反复观察同一个细节，清洗仪器，记录一些多年以后才有人翻看的数字。日常生活里的好奇心，多半是对小事的耐心。

paragraphs.en: Take the strangest accident in modern astronomy. In 1964, two young radio engineers, Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson, were testing a huge horn-shaped antenna in New Jersey. A soft hiss would not go away. They pointed the antenna at empty sky — the hiss stayed. They checked the wires, the amplifiers, the connections, everything they could think of.
paragraphs.zh: 以现代天文学中最奇特的一次意外为例。1964年，两位年轻的无线电工程师阿诺·彭齐亚斯和罗伯特·威尔逊正在新泽西州测试一台巨大的喇叭形天线。一种轻微的嘶嘶声始终不消失。他们把天线对准空旷的天空，那声音还在。他们检查了电线、放大器、接头，以及一切能想到的地方。

paragraphs.en: Then they discovered pigeons nesting inside the dish. They trapped the birds, cleaned out the nests and the droppings, and tried again. The hiss was still there. Many people would have called the machine broken and moved on to a different project. These two men kept asking. That unexpected noise turned out to be the oldest light in the universe, the faint echo of the Big Bang. They received the Nobel Prize in 1978.
paragraphs.zh: 后来他们发现，有鸽子在反射面里筑巢。他们捉住鸽子，清掉鸟巢和鸟粪，又重新测试。嘶嘶声依然存在。换作很多人，早就断定机器坏了，转去做别的项目。这两位却一直追问下去。那个出乎意料的噪音，结果是宇宙中最古老的光——大爆炸微弱的回声。1978年他们获得了诺贝尔奖。

paragraphs.en: Not every curious person is chasing a prize. Sometimes curiosity simply refuses to accept a clean, complete explanation. The chemist August Kekulé spent years puzzled by the shape of the benzene molecule, a problem that blocked an entire field. He later said the solution came to him while he was half asleep, dreaming of a snake biting its own tail. The closed ring was the missing piece.
paragraphs.zh: 并非每个好奇的人都在追逐奖项。有时候，好奇心只是拒绝接受一个干净又完整的答案。化学家奥古斯特·凯库勒为苯分子的形状困惑多年，这个问题卡住了整个领域。他后来说，答案是在半睡半醒之间来的，他梦见一条蛇咬住了自己的尾巴。那个闭合的环，正是缺失的那一块。

paragraphs.en: This kind of work demands patience as much as cleverness. Marie Curie and her husband spent four years in a cold, leaking shed, boiling tons of rock to separate less than a gram of radium. Nobody promised them success. They kept going because the next question was always more interesting than the last answer, and because a slow result they could trust felt better than a fast one they could not.
paragraphs.zh: 这类工作对耐心的要求，不亚于对聪明的要求。居里夫人和丈夫在一间寒冷漏风的棚屋里待了四年，煮沸成吨的矿石，只为分离出不到一克的镭。没有人向他们保证会成功。他们坚持下去，因为下一个问题总比上一个答案更有趣，也因为一个慢而可信的结果，胜过一个快却不敢信的结果。

paragraphs.en: Curiosity also has enemies. One is the fear of looking foolish in front of colleagues. Another is speed, because a quick answer feels more satisfying than an honest 'I don't know'. A third is pride: we naturally favour evidence that agrees with what we already believe. Careful scientists train themselves to notice when they badly hope a result is true, since that is exactly the moment they should doubt it.
paragraphs.zh: 好奇心也有敌人。一是怕在同事面前显得愚蠢；二是求快，因为一个快答案总比一句诚实的“我不知道”更让人舒服；三是自尊：我们天生偏爱那些和自己已有看法一致的证据。谨慎的科学家会训练自己留意：什么时候自己特别希望某个结果是真的——而那恰恰是最该怀疑它的时候。

paragraphs.en: The habit can be practised by anyone, at any age. Write your questions down before they vanish. Stay a little longer with a result that confuses you. Talk to people outside your own field, because their ordinary question may become your best idea. Clara Ma's single word is now crossing Mars, still sending home photographs of stones that nobody has named. Curiosity, it turns out, is a good name for a machine and a better one for a mind.
paragraphs.zh: 这种习惯任何人都能练，任何年龄都能练。趁问题还没消失，把它记下来；面对一个让你困惑的结果，多停留一会儿；和本行之外的人聊聊，因为他们随口一问，可能就是你最好的想法。克拉拉·马的那个词如今正穿越火星，不断把一块块无人命名过的石头的照片传回地球。看来，“好奇”这个名字，对一台机器来说很好，对一颗头脑来说更好。

questions.q: What did Penzias and Wilson do after they removed the pigeons and cleaned the antenna?
options: They sold the antenna to another laboratory.
They reported that the machine was completely broken.
They went on looking for the source of the noise.
They gave up radio astronomy and changed fields.
questions.explain: 细节题。第四段说他们捉住鸽子、清掉鸟巢和鸟粪后“tried again”，嘶嘶声仍在，而“These two men kept asking”，即他们继续追查噪声来源，因此选C。

questions.q: The phrase 'a clean, complete explanation' in paragraph 5 most probably means ______.
options: a final answer that leaves no question open
an explanation written in simple English
a reply given by a famous expert
a solution reached in a dream
questions.explain: 词义/句意题。第五段以凯库勒为例，说明好奇心“拒绝接受一个干净又完整的答案”，即拒绝接受那种看似把问题一次说清、不再留有余地的解释，故选A。

questions.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Curiosity is a childish quality that real scientists soon lose.
Curiosity is a working skill built on patience, doubt and attention to small details.
Almost all scientific discoveries come from dreams and accidents.
Scientists depend far more on luck than on training.
questions.explain: 主旨题。全文从“好奇号”命名出发，用彭齐亚斯与威尔逊、凯库勒、居里夫人等例子说明好奇心是耐心观察、追问异常、警惕自身偏见的职业能力，故选B。A、C、D均与文意不符或过度绝对。

questions.q: What can we infer from the last paragraph?
options: Only young students can develop a curious mind.
The Mars photographs are the greatest result curiosity has produced.
Asking people in other fields may help create new ideas.
Writing down questions is a waste of time.
questions.explain: 推断题。末段建议“Talk to people outside your own field, because their ordinary question may become your best idea”，可推知跨领域的提问有助于产生新想法，故选C。
